body_markdown:
A doom basket is a basket, bin, tote, or box for the random items that gather wherever life happens. Think hair ties, charging cords, sunglasses, books, pens, toys, and the one sock that keeps appearing on the coffee table.


The idea is simple: when a surface is covered in things you don’t feel like sorting right now, gather the loose items into one container. The area is clear again, and sorting can happen another time.


A doom basket isn’t a full[organizing system](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/organizing/how-to-stay-organized.html) . It’s a practical holding spot for the in-between stuff.


## Key Takeaways


- A doom basket gives loose clutter one place to land when you want to clear a surface quickly.
- It works well for small, dry household items that can wait to be put away.
- One basket in a high-clutter area can be more useful than a complicated organization plan.
- The goal is a usable space, not a perfectly styled home.


## Why the Doom Basket Method Works


Some clutter is easy to handle. A mug sitting in the kitchen sink. A jacket slung over the banister. Other items are harder because they belong somewhere else or seemingly showed up in the room without explanation.


That’s where a doom basket helps. It turns a scattered collection of little things into one contained collection of little things. Your coffee table, bedside table, or kitchen counter can work like a surface again instead of becoming a landing zone for every object that passed through the room.


It can also make how to[declutter your home](https://www.publicstorage.com/storage-solutions/decluttering) feel less dramatic. You don’t have to sort every item in a room before it looks better. Sometimes, gathering loose items into one basket is enough for now.


## What Can Go in a Doom Basket?


A doom basket works well for small household items that can wait to be put away.


**Items that work well in a doom basket:**


- Pens, chargers, hair ties, sunglasses
- Books, remotes, small accessories
- Things that belong in another room
- Small household odds and ends
- Spare change, socks, re-useable bags


If the basket becomes home to something you use every day, that’s useful information. That item may work better with a permanent spot nearby.


## Start With the Surface That Bothers You Most


You don’t have to begin with an entire room. Pick the one surface that makes you sigh when you walk past it.


Maybe it’s the entryway table covered in sunglasses, reusable bags, and small accessories. Maybe it’s the chair in your bedroom that has quietly become a second closet. Maybe it’s the bathroom counter, where products, hair tools, and random packaging seem to multiply overnight.


Clear that one spot, use the basket for the loose items, and enjoy the difference. One cleared surface can make a room feel more usable without turning the day into a full-house project.


## Give Everyday Items an Easy Place to Land


A doom basket can reveal which items tend to drift from room to room. Once you notice the pattern, a simple landing spot can help keep those things from returning to the same surface.


**If This Keeps Showing Up…** **Try This Nearby**


Keys, sunglasses, and small accessories A small tray near the door


Chargers and cords A drawer, pouch, or small box


Clothes worn once A hook, chair, or dedicated basket


Bathroom products A tray or bathroom organizer


Craft supplies A tote or project basket


Printed photos and keepsakes One labeled box for later sorting


For printed photos, the[best way to organize photos](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/organizing/photo-storage-and-organization-tips.html) is often to gather them in one place first. Sorting by year, event, or person can be a separate project another day. For now, one box is better than photos scattered across drawers and shelves.


## Keep the Basket Useful


A doom basket works best when it stays easy to carry and easy to see into. Choose something you can lift comfortably, then keep it where clutter tends to collect.


When it fills up, pull out the obvious things first. Return a book to its shelf. Move a charger to its drawer. Put away the sunglasses you were looking for yesterday. Let the remaining items wait until sorting sounds more appealing.


You can also swap a full basket for an empty one. It may sound a little chaotic, but it keeps the room from becoming cluttered again while leaving the first basket for later.


## Doom Basket Ideas for Different Rooms


**Room** **Container Idea** **What It Can Hold**


Entryway Small basket or tray Sunglasses, reusable bags, and small accessories


Living room Woven basket Remotes, books, cords, and blankets


Bedroom Tote or hamper Clothes, accessories, books, and small items


Bathroom Small bin or countertop tray Daily products and loose personal-care items


Craft area Project basket Pens, paper, yarn, scissors, and unfinished projects


A basket can work in the kitchen, too, as long as it stays away from food-prep areas. A small[kitchen organizer](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/organizing/kitchen-storage-ideas-9-photos.html) or tray can gather packets, pens, and other everyday extras that tend to collect on the counter.


## FAQs About the Doom Basket Method


**What is a doom basket?**


A doom basket is a temporary container for loose clutter that doesn’t have an immediate place. It can help clear a surface quickly while giving small items one place to wait.


**How do I use a doom basket to tidy up?**


Choose one cluttered surface, gather the small loose items into the basket, and put away obvious items when you feel like it. The basket holds the rest until you’re ready to sort it.


**Is a doom basket the same as organizing?**


Not exactly. A doom basket is a temporary way to contain clutter. It can make a room easier to use while you figure out where everyday items fit best.


## Let One Basket Handle the Loose Ends


A doom basket won’t make every item disappear, and that isn’t the point. It gives the little things that collect throughout the day one place to land, so your surfaces can work for you again.


When everyday clutter starts taking over the surfaces you use most, explore[Public Storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/) for organizing ideas that can help you create more room at home.
